author: M0M 0F 4

title: Preying on ADHD people. Beware
body:
What a shame. I really wanted to like this app and hoped it could make a real difference on how I manage my adhd symptoms. However following my experience with them, I cannot reach any other conclusion than thinking they are actually targeting the community they are supposed to help. 
In a few words, I tried the app for 2 solid months then decided it wasn’t working for me and cancelled my subscription. However instead of going ahead with it they sneakily stopped taking payments from my PayPal account and instead switched to taking payments directly through my bank debit card. This, without my consent or even informing me. I ended up paying an extra £364 over 13 months without realising it. When I asked them for a refund they just offered to refund 1 month - £28. Now I just spent 5 hours researching legal recourse, building my case and talking to my bank in the hope of getting my money back. And it’s just the beginning. How is that for helping people who naturally struggle handling administrative tasks and often miss details? I would say they are doing pretty well using their understanding of ADHD symptoms… against us. Please just beware.

Update: I was eventually given a full refund so I raise my rating a bit. However it took a lot of efforts and hours of complaining to the right places. And the cancellation process is still too unintuitive. I understand the need to generate income for startups but as an app for ADHDers, if you are really serious about helping us, ease of use and transparency about payments should be in your DNA. Please do better.

title: Maybe owned by ADHD staff but  triggering
body:

It was encouraging, and started to help understand about ADHD.  BUT - when asked to write a letter to myself when younger  and then discuss with the AI, i expressed that this was a possible trigger to PTSD, and explained how negative this module made me feel, the AI just moved on and wanted to ignore the issues that it had asked me to write about. 

Sadly after thinking about the cost of the monthly subscription, I decided to leave, why do you feel it’s appropriate to use my person module answers that I uploaded, as a tool to persuade me to stay, doesn’t that go against the core issues with ADHD, when we struggle to make decisions you throw back our answers, that’s just not right.  
And then to be offered a discount to stay, why don’t you offer this at the sign up, a lower montly cost, now I feel let down, and ripped off?

author: jamiepatrick17

title: Worth every penny.
body:
I have referred SO many of my friends to this app! 

I got curious if I had ADHD after struggling with what I call ‘chronic procrastination’. Unavoidable, crippling procrastination. Of work, of sleep, of contacting friends. 

While I was waiting for my diagnosis, I decided to try the app because if the shoe fits and it helps me, what’s the relevance of if I do or don’t have ADHD? (Spoiler: I do). 

If I could break my journey to where I am now down and how much better I can now work WITH and understand my adhd, this app contributed 70% of it. Easily.  

In the last 3 years, I’ve spent £10k on therapy and coaching from neuro divergent specialists, and that got me an extra 20% of the way. 

On reflection, it made me realise just how this app is worth every penny. 
I truly hope anyone reading this gives it a go and gets as much out of it as I have. 

One word of advice. You can lead a horse to water but you can’t force it drink. Ie. You get out of this app what you put in.
At least that’s what I found. 

All the best on your journey. It really is a gift to have adhd - even if it doesn’t always feel like it 🙏🏼

But for others it's worth a try, test it and it may suits you perfect. I'd recommend everyone to at least try it and see if it works for them.

body:
I am surprised how well this is working for me. I was t sure but decided to do a trial when I saw the quality of the advisors and team. I am so so so glad I did. 

I have read a lot about ADHD while waiting for my assessment. But now that I have a diagnosis I wanted to move forward in a more focussed way. 

Inflow is exactly what I needed to stop flitting around gathering random tips on the internet or in books. For now I feel like it’s doing the job of a coach and training and information all in one tight package.

Inflow brings a huge range of expertise together, presents it accessibly, and GUIDES you to act on it. This is a HUGE relief because it takes a load off my cognitive plate!! I have one place to go and it’s clear what to do.

I didn’t think I would like the AI chat part but I have it a try and it’s become a really useful part of the process. It’s almost like a guided coaching session with reflection with the goal setting and concrete change.

author: Anonymous 773

title: Predatory Free Trial - Be Careful
body:
Out of every free trial I’ve ever signed up for, this one has the most complex and misleading cancellation process. This is particularly alarming for an app that is supposedly founded and developed by experts in ADHD - and it’s clearly intentional because when they try to get you to sign up, they acknowledge that people with ADHD are more likely forget about their subscriptions and reassure you that they won’t let that happen. 

You might think that I’m exaggerating about how ridiculous the cancellation process is, but I assure you I’m not. Let me lay out the step-by-step process:

1. On the app, navigate to the ‘You’ page.

2. Click on the settings icon.

3. Now click on ‘Account 
Management and Help’. This opens up a separate webpage.

4. You now have to click on a link titled ‘How can I cancel my inflow subscription or free trial?’.

5. On this page, it gives 4-step instructions for cancelling your subscription. It fails to mention that there are more steps after the 4th step.

6. They also decide to mention here for the first time that if your trial ends in less than 24 hours, you can’t cancel it and you will be charged. There is no mention of this policy when signing up for the trial. In fact, it specifically states on the checkout page that you will be “Billed after your trial ends, unless cancelled before your renewal date.” which is objectively false - as you have to cancel one day before your renewal date to avoid being billed. 

If you are billed, you will have to now email them to request a refund. Despite claiming during the sign-up process that they’ll refund you if you forget to cancel your free trial, they fail to mention that you’re not entitled to a refund if you use the app after the renewal date - which most people likely will do if they don’t realise they’re trial has ended. Conveniently, they can also take up to 2 business days to respond to your refund request, meaning if you request a refund within the last 24 hours of your trial, but then use the app the next day while waiting for a response - you won’t be refunded.

7. If you’re lucky enough to be cancelling within the first 6 days - you now have to click a link to a new page called your ‘subscription portal’.

8. In this portal, you have to re-login using the password you made when you signed up. Many people will have forgotten it so they’ll have to reset it by questing a code by email. Weirdly, when I first logged into the app - I wasn’t asked if I wanted to ‘remember my password’ which I found odd - but I’m not sure if this was just my experience or the sign-up process is designed that way intentionally.

9. Once you’ve managed to log-in, click on the ‘manage my subscription’ heading for a new page with different options.

10. Now you click on the ‘cancel your subscription heading’. This is the 4th and final step listed in the instructions, but the team at inflow thought people with ADHD would appreciate it if the process was even longer, and more tedious - so they added some secret surprise steps. 

11. You now get a new page loaded up, asking if you are absolutely sure you want to cancel. The ‘Keep my subscription’ button is nice and bold, while the ‘cancel’ button is below and blends in perfectly with the background.

12. If you click this cancel button, surely that’s the end of it, right? It seems that way at first as a new page loads up with a “We’re sad to see you go.” message. Awww, how sweet of them to be sad that you’re gone.

13. Well actually, there is nothing to be sad about just yet!!! Because you haven’t gone!!! Your subscription is still not cancelled!!! 

14. You have to scroll down a little before you find the same exact buttons that were on the previous page. Now click ‘cancel’.

14. Another page! With the same two buttons! Click ‘cancel’ again.

15. I can now no longer remember if there were 3 or 4 of these pages in total - it wouldn’t surprise me if it were the latter, but at least now your subscription is actually cancelled, and you will not be billed.

Other subscription services do often make you put in extra effort to cancel, using similar sorts of tactics - but the fact that this was the most confusingly elaborate of them all, with so many opportunities to be mislead is just disturbing.

I suspect that if you looked into the companies financial statements, you’d find that payments from users that no longer use the app is a significant share of their total revenue.
author: Shdndjjsjshdhdh

title: Refunded, with no quibble
body:
I tried inflow on a 7 day trial. Easy to use, AI function is clever and bite sized lessons looked good.
I couldn’t justify the cost at this time and so planned to cancel within the trial period and… forgot! The App said they were ADHD friendly and would understand, but I was sceptical.
I emailed to request a refund. They promptly responded and one 30 second form later, my refund was authorised. In full. 
I had read lots of reviews where people struggled to get a refund. I hope my review brings some balance to this. If you intend to cancel within 7 days and go over by a few, they honour it.
Can’t say fairer than that.

author: alex.hertz

title: Ridiculous advice
body:
“You have ADHD. You struggle with time management. Have you tried… not struggling?” is the gist of every “lesson”. 

Time blindness - oh don’t worry, just get a few more clocks, then you’ll be fine. I don’t struggle to KNOW the time?! I struggle to understand when to move from one task to the next, when it’s too late for me to get somewhere on time… it’s not just “oh look, it’s 4pm, I have an appointment at 4:30pm, best leave now” and the struggle is magically fixed 🤣 

A *real* quote from a lesson I just read is “ADHD doesn’t have to be in the driver’s seat of your life. You can take the wheel now. Where you go next is up to you.” Oh gee, thanks Dr Patronising. Hadn’t thought of that in my silly little ADHD brain. Of course, the answer is just to make different choices!! Doh! 

For £40 / month, I’d expect to at least not be patronised. Do better.
author: Kaylaaa737064280

title: If I could give 0 stars I would
body: This app markets itself as being a management tool for ADHD…so far all I’ve managed to find are condescending “lessons” for me to learn about a condition I’ve had for nearly 40 years!🙄🤣 all I wanted was an efficient calendar and to do list and time management tools all in one app cos no one seems to have come up with that despite telling us “they’re thinking of people who struggle with ADHD” in the design and purpose of this app!🤣 oh and then there are lots of “don’t worry we’ll remind you before we charge you if you forget to cancel your subscription”…then a yearly charge on your card when you think it’s cancelled as they have different sections that you have to navigate your way to in order to do this rather than appearing in Apple subscriptions even if you’ve downloaded the app and paid by Apple Pay!!! When I requested a refund rather than just issuing it I now have had 3 emails and been sent a form to fill in…is your company really tailoring its services to people with ADHD or just targeting them as easy cash?!😡
author: Vix2475

title: Charged me $199.99 despite cancelling before end of trial period
body:
And are now refusing to refund me because the grace period mentioned in their refund policy has passed. Never mind that this is irrelevant since I already cancelled! They claim I didn’t, that they didn’t hear back from me when they sent a reminder email, and that “it's possible that the message ended up in your spam folder”. I actually check my spam folder regularly so I know nothing went there. Besides, none of their emails have ever gone to spam, why this one? And indeed if I didn’t cancel but instead paid $200 for the app - whose material I didn’t find particularly helpful - you’d think I’d at least use it. I only opened it during the trial week and yesterday when I saw the charge on my foreign bank account. They also had the nerve to tell me they’ll offer me a free annual subscription as a way to make up for the frustration. No. I don’t want your app. I didn’t find it helpful so I cancelled before the end of the trial period. You charged me all the same (I’m not alone in this btw). This is the crux of the issue, setting aside reminder emails and regace periods and spam folders and whatnot.
It is unacceptable. I expect I’ll get a developer response rehashing the same claims and offers, instead of doing the single right and sensible thing: refunding me for the hefty fee. I’ll be reporting them.
PS: The fact that there is a) no notification sent pre or post charge (not even a generic email saying “thank you for your subscription, you now have access to abc resources until xyz date” etc) and b) choosing to automatically charge an ANNUAL subscription fee, not monthly, quarterly etc, for an ADHD support app tells you all you need to know about them.
author: nope nope2024

title: Helpful

author: Nina.Katya

title: Yeah… no…
body: It’s hard to justify the cost of the subscription when the core of the content is just the same info and tools that you can learn online for free or from any mental health councillor if you see one. Everyone, who’s been trying to address procrastination, messy home, disorganisation and overwhelm, heard about pomodoro technique or SMART goals and chances are, they don’t really work, otherwise there would be no need for yet another app peddling the same tired techniques. No need to pay over 180 quid a year to get the same content. There’s some social aspect to the app but I haven’t explored that other than some daily questions. What this app does is to give you some info and some quizzes about it but if you’re really looking for a good tool to help stay organised and on top of things then I suggest Strides - it’s free, you can trial it for free, you can subscribe for extra templates but what it does, it actually helps you manage your daily life. At least the cancellation process has been fixed and I wasn’t charged after I cancelled the trial.
author: CheshireTheCat13

author: VDisappointed2024

title: Unhelpful
body:
The app hasn’t told me anything I don’t already know under the Burnout module, what I need are the tools to put those things in place. How am I supposed to choose what things can be sacrificed in my life if I don’t have anyone I can delegate tasks to or ask for help? How do I abandon my vulnerable elderly mother with dementia to make “me time”?
It’s unrealistic advice because it assumes that it’s all our own fault and the things we take on can be set aside, but that’s not always the case and there is no deviation in the advice to help you determine what things can be set aside  and what the priorities are. I’m deeply disappointed because I’d really hoped this would be a turning point for me but I’m back at square one.
author: Happycookie20000000000

author: Sumpte.

title: Don’t bother signing up if you just want to demo it for free with no commitments
body:
The app is stuck behind a paywall so once you go through the arduous process of giving all of your personal details and answer questions about your ADHD, verify with a code sent via email etc etc etc 

You get a message saying you’ll be charged if you don’t cancel after you free charge (although you can supposedly email the team and request a refund..).

The annual subscription cost is far too greedy -£200 a year / £50 a month, for what the app can actually offer. 

For someone with adhd wanting to see if this will actually be helpful, or just another lost expense in the pursuit of adhd support, this isn’t isn’t the app for me.

There should be more transparency from the start about the very high cost, and also, more thought given to a demo/free trial.

author: Fab Product

title: Double charged me and no response
body:
App is ok. Some nice messaging and framing of things in there. 

I found the UX a little clunkier. I wanted to complete sections and progress, but was asked to reflect on the week I’d had like I was doing an exercise each day, although actually I was burning through the module in one (hyper focused) go. 

Also, somehow they ended up charging me twice, via App Store and directly. No response via support, which is a bit rubbish.

body: It’s just for money it’s not free
author: henrbrbrvrb

body:
Once you’ve completed ALL of your details and filled a questionnaire in, you’re then hit with the 7 day free trial with no pricing info at all. Never mentioned in any sponsored ad’s and now they have all my info. Completely deceptive. 
Absolutely scam.
author: Cer318

title: Could be a bit better
body: I have only been using it a couple of days and so far it seems to have good content. Just one criticisms, on apple devices, for past webinars you can’t see which ones you have played ves which ones you haven’t. And if you had to stop in the middle of one, the app does not save where you left off so you can return to the same point
author: Basque in London

title: Now too expensive
body: I used this app last year and thought it amazing it really helped me a lot, the information in it and the explanations for why our brains work in certain ways and how to avoid ADHD pit falls are very good. But unfortunately they have increased the price to a point where I can no longer afford it. If you can afford it get it, but they have priced themselves out of me.
author: Gtmforge

title: Payment taken after cancellation
body: I downloaded this app without realising it would be a paid subscription. I looked at the free trial and then immediately cancelled the subscription as it did not seem worth the annual fee. The app then took the subscription payment from my bank anyway! This has left me very short of funds and waiting the 2 days they take to respond before even generating a refund which will take several days no doubt to come through if they even will agree to a refund. Really disappointed and inconvenienced by the whole thing.
author: Anna.flower

title: Poor CX ruins the app
body: I cancelled this subscription as soon as I set up the trial as I knew I would forget otherwise (and I could always reinstate if needed at a later date). I got very quick confirmation of this being cancelled so was very pleased. It was a busy week so I wasn’t able to utilise the trail, a real shame, yet at the end of the week I was still charged £159(!) I find this really upsetting as I did everything needed to avoid this happening and was told it wouldn’t happen… and still! Very upsetting and I hope I don’t have to wait too much longer for this to be resolved.
author: Mrs_Scarf

title: support system section is bad & subscription is deceptive
body:
absolutely detestable design. apps that don’t tell you it will cost money until you have completed a quiz and should be BANNED. say this on the opening screen. this is deceptive design and not acceptable

also - why is sibling not an option?? or cousin?? these are my main support systems. this should be an option, or people should be able to select “other”. it feels EXTREMELY limiting and VERY exclusionary. allowing an “other” option is UX 101 - this should NOT have made it past going live!!!!!
author: lou23847328943

title: Not ADHD friendly
body: Confusing layout, walls of text, not great for someone with ADHD and a short attention span. Really annoying. I open the app, get overwhelmed with all the stuff it wants me to do and close it. Need to make it more rewarding / dopamine inducing.
author: Appism

title: Do not fall for the Scam!!
body: I did the 1 week trial. Was told by the app it will send reminders to cancel the subscription days before it ends and then never got any reminders. So ofcourse the app then charged me £159. Struggling with ADHD means we’re not going to remember to cancel these sort of things hence the reminders that were needed. They know what they’re doing! Praying on us poor ADHD people to giving them the money. I’ve tried emailing already and requesting a refund but have had no response. I demand a refund. Absolutely useless!
author: JaySlay666

title: Predatory business model. Avoid
body: However much they claim to ‘understand’ people with ADHD, they clearly don’t. A misleading free trial,  NO email reminders when you’re about to be charged (contrary to their claims) and the app is incredibly frustrating to use. Just a terrible experience all round.
author: LKX236

title: Paid only
body:
Don’t be lured in if you don’t have money to burn it’s trying to sell you your mental health for £200 a year or £50 a month. there’s nothing available for people struggling to get by.

*update: you’re committed to profiting from mental health struggles you’re not committed ti helping everyone otherwise you’d include an affordable option, rather than a waiting list/access programme that I bet you would share any stats on about application:award ratios.
author: Nxl Jxb

title: Subscription taken incorrectly
body: I always immediately cancel subscriptions so was shocked when a charge came through.  When I went on the app, it flashed up my subscription was cancelled but when I logged in it was set up for monthly subscriptions.  When I checked on my subscriptions through my iPhone, it isn’t listed as a live or cancelled subscription so I was unable to ensure it was cancelled via subscriptions in my settings.  I would definitely advise against downloading this app unless they have a reasonable explanation for this.  Have asked for my money back but as I can’t see it in descriptions, I am concerned about being charged again next month…
author: ShezzaJane

title: Couldn’t sign up
body: Got through the whole onboarding but only to get an “it’s not you, it’s us” error. If you’re going to create an app for people who have ADHD then sort stuff like this out because some will do exactly what I did - Delete it because it’s too much bother. I’m brilliant at self sabotaging and procrastination - I don’t need an excuse NOT to do something, so this was the perfect reason to dump the app. Doh.

title: Difficult to cancel

author: lmn8134

title: Free-trial then take your money
body:

As an App that tries to help ADHD people, they sure try to put a lot of obstacles to get u a refund and to opt automatically to their full year subscription which is £179 per year and make it difficult for you to get a refund. author: mccalling

title: A life saving app
body: This app is genius. So much live accountability. So much bite sized wisdom. So we’ll put together. Everyone needs this app. Especially if you have ADHD. And even if you don’t!

I’ve deleted app have no sign of subscription on my phone … idk how to stop them from charging me every month?

body: I’ve had to cancel my subscription twice now, signed up for free trial but didn’t work for me so cancelled and deleted app. Now found that my subscription hadn’t cancelled and been charged the full amount. body:
This app seems like it waffles along, started the trial and didn’t get as far as getting any help from it. A week is too short. I logged out and removed the app as advised and still charged. No where in the app can you cancel the payment. It’s seems really easy to install and take your money but really difficult to stop the subscription. It’s a con. Please refund me.

author: Aaronembe

title: Subscription needed
body: Installed the app, went through a bunch of info etc only to find you need a subscription to actually use it. More transparency is needed on the app page.
author: Littleowl91

title: Life changing
body: Full disclosure, I was lucky enough to get this app through the access programme as I was struggling with my employment at the time. I wasn’t in a great place, and neither was my mental health. This app has really helped me understand myself and learn how to cope with my ADHD. I’ve been constantly amazed to learn how many things I struggle with aren’t all that unique to me and instead are pretty common symptoms. Daily sessions are just 5 minutes. At first I thought this was a bit insubstantial, but its actually the perfect amount to fit in around a commute and as it doesn’t seem like a big commitment, I’m much more likely to engage on a routine basis. After 9 months of using the app I’ve seen a lot of improvement in aspects of my life such as emotional regulation, time keeping and organisation. My ADHD does still make things harder, but in general I’m far more accepting & forgiving of myself, and my relationships with others are a lot healthier.
author: wilkovic

title: Could not get through the first lesson

UI is confusing.
author: Susoku

title: Not particularly helpful
body: I was hoping for something that could help me overcome my ADHD issues, however the advice and information given was very basic, I have already implemented most of the strategies given and most of them don’t work for me particularly well, there was no alternatives, the advice seems to use the reward theory a lot, but this isn’t helpful if you are not a person who responds to ‘rewards’ and gets no motivation from them. The multi choice questions aren’t particularly multi choice, I regularly found that none of the options described my feelings or situation, all in all I just got more irritated and frustrated the more I tried to work thru the modules. I wouldn’t mind paying for this if it would help in any way but for me there was nothing particularly helpful.
author: katejjjjjjj

title: really working content in bite chunks!
body:

Also it's beautifully done, information is bite chunked, doing just 5 minutes a day in the evening seems to work for me!
author: Alex Turkin

title: Warning: Deceptive Pricing Practices in this App!
body: I installed this app expecting to try out a free trial, but what I encountered was a pricing strategy that left me baffled and frustrated. To access the so-called “free trial,” you’re required to commit to a hefty £180 annual payment, but only if you pay it all at once. If you can’t afford that upfront, be prepared to face an astonishing charge of £516. In essence, it’s £180 for the privileged few and a staggering £516 for the rest of us. And here’s the kicker: if you forget to cancel before the free trial ends, you’ll be hit with unexpected charges. Don’t be fooled by smooth-talking responses from the company. While they claim to offer refunds if you forget to cancel, that might not be a lifeline for everyone. For some, the damage is already done when they can’t afford to pay for groceries at the checkout. It’s clear and straightforward: if they truly wanted to provide a genuine free trial, they could do so without these financial traps. They could charge everyone fairly, regardless of their ability to pay upfront. My advice? Exercise caution and think twice before getting involved with this app.
author: BOK Karl

title: £199 for an App!
body: Spent 10 minutes answering questions before you get to the part where they want to rob you
author: ADHDDAN

title: Ridiculously expensive
body: £33 a month is just too much
author: XXChris

title: An hour in and I’m ready to cry
body:
There are many issues with this app right from the start. They create roadblock after roadblock that any neurotypical would be able to navigate with ease but for us neurospicy individuals it’s like walking over hot coals, while trying to carry a car, In a crowded room with everyone talking. LOUD. 

Once you have downloaded the app you have to go through the signup process and there we reach the first roadblock. I have to pick a username, out of thin air, with no context of how it will be used. 

The app won’t let you continue without picking one, they won’t assign a random one for you, you have to create one. Without any limits or rules displayed. 

If you make it past this point (which took me nearly 15 minutes) you then have to agree to either a yearly billing or monthly billing. And yes I know they say there is a 7 day free trial and also if you forget to cancel they will refund you but do they not release we have RSD. 

Just the idea in our own heads that we may be rejected for a refund will make us not ask for it. Yes I know they guarantee it no questions asked but we still think it’ll get rejected (that’s why it’s a dysphoria). Another thing you think they would understand since the creators claim to have ADHD themselves. 

Moving in from that and this was the last straw for me. To be able to do anything in the app you HAVE to watch a video of a guy talking to you.  NO NO NO NO NO. I immediately shut the app down and uninstalled it. 

To say this app is supposed to have been created by neurodivergent developers it’s my absolute nightmare and looking at other reviews I’m not the only one.
author: Yorkshire Hot Tub Services

title: This app changed my life. Seriously.
body: After i got ADHD diagnosis it felt great to have an explanation for why things in my life are the way they are but then i had to take action. This was paralysing. I watched YouTube videos and spoke to people on Reddit but only made small amounts of progress. This app is a gem, it has loads of educational content and an ADHD coach who is amazing. She doesn’t answer back immediately but it’s fast enough to not be an issue. I will be a lifelong user!
author: plandrover1

title: Ok. Expensive & Coaching is not good for the price.
body:
I like to community aspect of this app. I like the courses that you can do and the zoom ‘drop-ins’. However the big USP of this app is the personal coaching. 

This is why they charge £170 per year. However the coach I had would send scripted sentences about setting goals about 2 days after I sent them a message. 

I was struggling at one point and didn’t respond to a few messages and haven’t heard from them since (about 4 months ago), no check-ins, or queries about how things were going. Nada. 

I like the idea behind this app. However I do feel like I’ve paid hugely over the odds for what is essentially a few very brief 5 min Education courses.

title: Great app

It would be better to provide limited access for free and allow people to opt in to the paid service rather than forcing a subscription that has to be cancelled on people who are trying to get help with organisation. Seems like an unfair and very expensive trap to me. I deleted it immediately as I know I’ll forget to cancel. Plus it’s not worth it if you only get 1 week free.
author: Metsuzy

title: Rip off
body: Won’t even let you start without a 7 day trial and then charges £50 a month!!! Absolute rip off.
author: velleity18

title: Deleted the App!
body:
Downloaded this app before founding out it costs £180 per year to use. 

As there is only a 7 day free trial to see if this expensive App is worth all the money (not long enough) and knowing I will most likely forget to cancel if I don’t find it usefull - I have decided to delete it before even getting started. 

I have no problem paying money for something that’s good but how do we know unless we’ve tried it out.

If you are truly confident in your App - make the free trial longer - 30 days - and this is the most important thing you need to do - DON’T TAKE ANY PAYMENT DETAILS UNTIL THE END OF THE TRIAL. You will then gain trust from the beginning and more people will try it out. 

If it’s good we will pay. If not we won’t. What you are doing is unscrupulous for people with ADHD - you are taking advantage of the people you are supposedly helping. Shame on you.

title: Not helpful at all
body: Going in, I expected this app to try and support my short attention span, improve my focus and generally help with my symptoms of adhd. The layout of the login process was not clear at all, complicated, hard to navigate and time consuming. The app does not let you in unless you commit to a 7 days free trial, at the end which the app will automatically start charging you if you forget to cancel. They do say that they’ll refund you if you forget to cancel, but as with a lot of other apps, verifying such things can be incredibly time consuming and complicated, not something that people with adhd need to deal with. Please devs, if you actually want to help people like myself at all, change the login process! I deleted this app pretty soon after getting it and will not be redownloading.
author: LangleyHQ

title: Terribly expensive

author: garavatito

title: Do you even know how adhd people suffer? Doesn’t appear so.
body:
I have 2 major issues from the get go with this app. First, it’s too expensive, the majority of people with adhd struggle with our finances as a result of impulsive or inattentive behaviour, when I looked at reviews they were saying £20 a month £90 a year, and I thought that was ok, only to go through sign up and find it’s double that, £43 a month or £180 a year. £43 is what I spend on my whole food shop for a week for my household of 2! No app, which has major limitations and cannot replace actual coaching, especially for a condition where accountability is a major driving issue, is worth that much money. They say it’s to replace in person coaching but frankly, you can not to open an app, you can ignore reminders, and more often than not they become wallpaper as they mix with all the other notifications on your phone. You can’t ignore a person who is actually stood there asking how something went. Plus when looking at reviews the things that might make it worth the exorbitant cost are not in my time zone.

Second, Promising to refund people who forget to cancel isn’t good enough, you should have a free trial that is actually free, no payment details taken until the trial is over. It’s shocking that as you claim to have adhd yourselves you don’t do a trial where no details are taken, and knowing that the majority of adhd people will 1. Forget to ask for a refund, and 2. Procrastinate on it when they do remember because it’s so much painful admin is predatory and frankly disgusting. Of all people you should know how hard it is to remember to cancel at a time that you can actually cancel, and not remember while you’re washing up or driving the car, and you should know that as time goes on people are going to build a wall of awful around cancelling. 
If you actually believed your app was as good as you claim and wanted to be inclusive you would be like sunsama, have a 14 day free trial where people can try it without having to give you payment details or set up a payment, then they try the app and love it and find it useful so they then pay. If you’re so sure your app is so great what have you got to lose? Surely everyone who tries it will want to pay for it because it’s so amazing it’s worth spending the same amount I spend on groceries every month?
Alternatively you could set it up so that if the person doesn’t use the app for say 5 days in a row, it automatically cancels and refunds them, why don’t you do that instead of manipulating the very condition you claim to support?
author: GECarr

title: Amazing tool for recently diagnosed adult with ADHD
body: Inflow is so much more than just another ADHD app. Yes, it is expensive, but definitely cheaper than going to an ADHD coach or seeing a therapist even once a month. It’s a personal, real person, qualified coach who you can reach out to about questions or for accountability. It’s a resourceful place with plenty of useful modular courses on subjects such as acceptance, women and girls with ADHD, relationships, procrastination, etc. Everyone of them broken into short texts with audio recordings (by a human) of around 4-6 minutes. You can listen to/read one each day, reflect on it in a little text box after (if you want to) and get some helpful tips that you can save for future reference.    This app also offers live video links that you can join to keep you accountable and on-task when you want to accomplish something (homework, chores, work, etc). There are also live video discussions with psychologists and other specialists that you can join on various subjects. These are so helpful to see that you are not alone! And the community section as well where we can exchange on struggles and successes. Finally, you get several challenge ideas and guidance to learn new tactics, improve some habits or routines, etc. One thing though, I noticed that the “Daily Flow” isn’t there anymore. Please bring it back! It’s one of the best things in Inflow! It is what gets me motivated to open the app and gets me started on the modules. If you won’t put it back on the home page, can we have a way to access the previous ones? I have tried many guided meditation/reflection apps and this is the best for me. Thank you Dr. Sachs and the Inflow team!

body:

title: Tone is not quite right.
body:
Now that the technical issues have been fixed, I’ve had the chance to give this a go. The structure of the app and chunking of the information is great. I love that there are both video and text options. The information itself is brilliant… and there are definitely techniques that I could learn and use to help manage my time and support my organisation. 

However, the language used is disappointing, and the tone is not quite right for me. In one section alone there is reference to “messing up”, “screw ups” and “weakness”. Not everyone’s experience with ADHD has been negative, and I’m not sure how helpful this narrative is.
author: Icclemoose

title: Also disappointed
body:

author: LilRockit

title: Disappointed
body:
I really hate when you download an app that does not state that if you want to use it at all, you have to enter into a yearly subscription (nearly £90). Yes you get a 7 day free trial but as someone with ADHD, I often forget to cancel these and then end up paying for something I might use. Also, I had to go through the whole verification/account set-up process with emails and confirmation codes and emails that take too long too arrive so that was super frustrating and made me wonder if the developers actually know anyone with ADHD or realise how frustrating these kind of multi-step processes are for someone with ADHD. 

So I never got to use the app, but if these basics aren’t right for someone with ADHD then how good can the actually app even be!
author: MummyMelsa

title: Useful practical help
body: I’ve only used this app for the free trial so far but I’ve really enjoyed it. The daily coaching is full of useful tips and these are presented as challenges to motivate you to complete it. The app is really accessible - at first I was dismayed that the coaching session were audio but there’s options to alter voice speed and there’s a text instead option, and all the sessions are short and concise and summarised at the end.
author: Ixuxia

title: Good if you aren’t in therapy/don’t have other resources
body: I was hoping that this app would offer helpful routine/time management things, like letting you plan a routine, timers/reminders, offering resources on how to develop and stick to routines, etc. That’s not really what it’s for – it’s basically a therapy programme which has a journal & a space for you to write what you want to focus on every day. The therapeutic resources are OK – I imagine there are probably a few things in there that I didn’t already know, but I’ve covered a lot of it in CBT, DBT and other therapies I’ve done or read about independently. So if you’re a beginner to emotional regulation, time management, etc. and/or just want to put some work in across the board, it’s probably good for that, but it’s quite beginner-level so I won’t be paying for the full version after the trial. A lot of potential and I’ll be keeping an eye out for updates, but this version didn’t offer me anything new.
author: nickyjwatkinson

title: Life changing
body: This is a great app and programme, and unique as far as I can tell. It is helping me get to grips with some of the most frustrating and paralysing aspects of ADHD in a way that I have not been able to do with other resources. It’s divided into small sections which I find perfect for my attention span - on most days I simply can’t take in more, and I find I can apply the tips and suggestions given quite easily and effectively. Sometimes I forget all about the app but then after a few days I return and pick up where I left off - there’s no pressure. Finally the app is also special because it is interactive, not just a bit of inanimate  software. The developers are clearly engaged and present, including through live Q&As with the experts. Many thanks to the creators of this app.
author: Rakooo9771xx

title: Amazing
body:
I joined inflow in a time where I was at my lowest and had no idea what to do with myself or how to act especially since my adhd has just been getting out of hand and too overwhelming. Inflow is truly amazing and honestly makes me feel so much more confident with my adhd and mostly, makes me know that I am not alone and heard. I actually really love the Q&A as it makes it more personal and allows me to get an answer from a professional and not just google, as well as hear other people’s questions which may be useful for me too. 

The modules are really helpful especially with the challenges they provide, it actually makes me have to do the thing rather than just listen to something and never try it. It also helps keep things exciting for the adhd brain because completing a challenge or a module is just exciting and makes you feel like you did something that day.

However, one thing I would say is that is that I wish others could access this app without having to pay. I fully understand that the creators worked really hard for this and dedicated so much time, effort and money to make this and they also have bills to pay however some people may really need help just like I did when everything just got too overwhelming for me. I was able to get some help from this app but others may not be able to depending on their situation which really saddens me. However I wish that in the future this app could become free or even allow some people (depending on their situation and financial state) to access this app for free. I truly think that anyone should be able to get the help they need when they need it which is why I hope something could be done in the future.

Overall amazing as an app and I fully support it and would definitely recommend!
author: its_Sama9811

title: it’s a great app!!
body: I love inflow and i definitely think it’s worth trying!
author: betealb

title: Really good app
body: I joined the beta group for this and found the app good. I don’t use it daily but I have found the content ADHD-friendly and there’s no built in ‘pressure’ to use it consistently -or streaks to lose- but lots of good tips and useful wisdom.
author: salsapinkkat

title: Really helpful to support people with ADHD
body: The different modules offer practical ways to improve many symptoms and manifestations of ADHD. You can do the programme at your own pace and it does not take a lot of time.
author: Dungamaria

title: Great tool for people with ADHD
body:
I recommend Inflow to anyone who has ADHD. Great tools for both self understanding & also setting up effective coping strategies/habits. 

As a professional working with adults with ADHD I shall be recommending it to my clients.
author: Lifecatalyst

title: Great!
body: Really helpful app, great tips and fantastic meditation.
author: Cornell Busch Beth CDC

title: Misleading.
body:
At first glance this app looks great. A free app with great reviews, for people with ADHD that are trying to get their lives in order.

During onboarding I get to tell you about myself and choose how I’d like to be supported. After setting up an account I’m presented with a screen telling me that nothing is free. Nothing can be tried and no help is available –unless I agree to spend as much as £25. Every month!

It can’t be dismissed and I have no way of removing my account. This is the most misleading and underhand of approaches. After such high hopes it seems only those that have plenty of disposable income get help.

Find out how much people can really afford to pay. A private diagnosis and titration (given overstretched and under commissioned NHS services) costs around £1000. An extra £300/year for this app (on top of prescription costs) is exclusive, discriminatory and desperately unfortunate.

I’d like to remove my account, and all the answers I provided, from your systems.
author: Smarthome fan

title: Helpful
body: Love the supportive voices and I find the daily challenges very helpful!
